source_basis: Opening sentence: 'Facing the increasingly close cooperation and connection in modern society, it has become an important development direction of modern data science.'
interpretation: Double L2 calque: participial 'Facing' (面对) + 'development direction' (发展方向). Native English would use 'Given [trend], [field] has increasingly focused on.' Very high authenticity signal.
applicability: Reusable for any D-type abstract opener: Facing [growing trend], it has become [direction/focus] to [goal].
counterevidence: Native speakers occasionally use 'Facing' participially but never pair it with 'development direction'.

source_basis: 'In this way' used as section-closing connector on pages 1, 7, 8, 11, 14, 16, 17, 19 — seven or more occurrences across the paper.
interpretation: Extreme frequency of 这样 calque as paragraph/section closure. Native writers vary with 'thus', 'accordingly', 'in doing so'. Repetition count itself is L2 marker.
applicability: Track In-this-way frequency per paper as L2 intensity metric. Any count above 3 in a 20-page paper is unusual.
counterevidence: Some native technical writers do repeat 'In this way' but rarely more than twice in a paper.

source_basis: 'has become a key link in the technical analysis of modern football'
interpretation: 成为关键环节 calque. 'Key link' is a direct translation of 关键环节; native English prefers 'central step', 'crucial component', or 'key element'.
applicability: Reusable across all types: 'has become a key link in [field]' as significance claim.
counterevidence: 'Key link' appears occasionally in native English but typically refers to chain/sequence, not general importance.

source_basis: 'The study of Duch J et al. used the method of network analysis...' followed by sequential author-by-author citations.
interpretation: Author-chain literature survey rather than thematic grouping. Each citation introduced with 'The study/research/literature of [Author] et al.' Common L2 pattern from Chinese academic writing.
applicability: Reusable for introduction sections: sequential author-chain with 'The study of [A] used [M] to [V]' template.
counterevidence: Thematic organization is standard in native English reviews; author-by-author is not wrong but marks L2 training.

source_basis: 'we make a broken line chart of the use times of each tactic in each game'
interpretation: 折线图 (zhéxiàntú) literal translation. Standard English: 'line chart' or 'line graph'. 'Broken line chart' is a very strong L2 signal — AI would never produce this.
applicability: High-value human marker. Include in language skill as visualization reference: 'broken line chart' = L2 for 'line chart'.
counterevidence: 'Broken line' has a math meaning (piecewise linear) but 'broken line chart' is not standard terminology.

source_basis: 'our possession rate is in the ascendant'
interpretation: Register error: 'in the ascendant' is archaic/astrological English. L2 writer selected it as a formal synonym for 'dominant' or 'higher'. AI would never choose this register.
applicability: Record as register-selection error pattern. Useful for mimicking genuine L2 register mistakes in generated text.
counterevidence: 'In the ascendant' exists in English but is associated with astrology/literary contexts, not sports analytics.

source_basis: 'This indicator comes from the literature of Cintia et al. After reading the literature, we believe the Pezzali score is indeed an excellent indicator'
interpretation: Unusual citation phrasing with personal endorsement: 'After reading, we believe... is indeed excellent.' Native writers cite without such explicit approval language.
applicability: Reusable as source-attribution pattern with personal endorsement: comes-from + after-reading + we-believe.
counterevidence: Native academic writing avoids 'after reading' as obvious and 'we believe' as subjective in formal context.

source_basis: Table 4 contains 'Variance pf players' passing volume'
interpretation: Preposition typo: 'pf' for 'of'. Characteristic L2 keyboard error not caught by spellcheck (adjacent keys). AI text generation would never produce this typo.
applicability: Record as typo-class L2 marker. Valuable for authenticity: keyboard adjacency errors in prepositions.
counterevidence: Native speakers also make typos but usually catch 'pf' in table headers.

source_basis: 'We can intuitively observe the obvious positive correlation between TAI and GD from the graph'
interpretation: 直观地观察 (zhíguān de guānchá) literal translation. Native English: 'clearly see' or 'readily observe'. 'Intuitively observe' conflates visual clarity with intuition.
applicability: Reusable as visual-evidence connector: 'intuitively observe [X] from the graph, which proves [Y]'.
counterevidence: 'Intuitively' in native English means 'by gut feeling', opposite of the intended 'visually obvious'.

source_basis: 'we stripe it out to make the mean value reasonable'
interpretation: Malapropism: 'stripe' (decorate with stripes) for 'strip' (remove). L2 spelling/vocabulary confusion between similar-sounding English words. AI would never make this error.
applicability: High-value human marker. Record stripe/strip confusion as L2 vocabulary error pattern.
counterevidence: Native speakers might write 'strip' correctly or use 'remove' instead; 'stripe it out' is uniquely L2.

source_basis: 'we are 90% sure that with the normal fluctuation of the Pezzali indicator, TAI value will fall within the interval'
interpretation: L2 confidence phrasing: 'we are 90% sure' instead of native 'we can be 90% confident'. Personalizes statistical statement.
applicability: Reusable for sensitivity sections: 'we are [X]% sure' as L2 alternative to 'at the [X]% confidence level'.
counterevidence: Some informal native writing uses 'sure' but not in formal statistical reporting.

source_basis: 'there is a mutual restraint between different formations'
interpretation: 相互制约 (xiānghù zhìyuē) calque. Native English: 'counterbalance', 'trade-off', or 'rock-paper-scissors dynamic'. 'Mutual restraint' sounds like a legal/physical constraint.
applicability: Record as domain-transfer calque: 'mutual restraint' for competitive interaction between strategies.
counterevidence: 'Mutual restraint' exists in nuclear arms context but not in sports/game theory.

source_basis: 'our work innovatively proposed to analyze the main tactics based on the 15min time interval'
interpretation: Self-praise adverb '创新性地提出' (chuàngxīnxìng de tíchū) calque. Native academic English avoids 'innovatively' as self-description; would say 'we propose a novel approach'.
applicability: Reusable for strengths sections: 'innovatively proposed' as L2 self-praise pattern.
counterevidence: Native writers use 'novel' or 'new' but rarely adverbially modify 'proposed' with 'innovatively'.

source_basis: 'our work can't reach the detailed analysis of the tactics on the pitch'
interpretation: 无法达到 (wúfǎ dádào) calque: 'can't reach' for 'cannot achieve' or 'falls short of'. Spatial metaphor transferred inappropriately.
applicability: Record as inability-expression calque: 'can't reach [analysis level]' for 'cannot attain/achieve'.
counterevidence: Native writers would never say 'can't reach the analysis'; they'd say 'cannot perform' or 'is unable to achieve'.

source_basis: 'we can refer to the building method of the model, to build up a comprehensive evaluation system'
interpretation: 参考建模方法 (cānkǎo jiànmó fāngfǎ) calque: 'refer to the building method' for 'adopt the modeling approach'. Awkward verb choice.
applicability: Record as method-transfer calque: 'refer to the building method' for 'draw on the approach'.
counterevidence: Native English uses 'refer to' for looking up information, not for adopting a methodology.

source_basis: Team structure modeled via undirected weighted passing network: nodes=players, edges=passes. Arrow width encodes pass count, circle size encodes player activity.
interpretation: Standard network-analysis approach for team sports. Undirected assumption loses directional information but simplifies analysis.
applicability: Reusable for any team-interaction network. Pattern: define nodes/edges from event data, visualize with edge width and node size.
counterevidence: Directed networks capture tactical asymmetry better but require more data preprocessing.

source_basis: TAI constructed from 6 factors (P, H, R1-R4) via entropy weight method. Objective data-driven weighting.
interpretation: EWM provides objective weights without expert judgment. Pezzali dominates (35.75%), H indicator weakest (8.42%). Independence assumption may not hold.
applicability: EWM composite index reusable for any multi-factor evaluation. Pattern: standardize → entropy → weight → linear combination.
counterevidence: Principal component analysis or factor analysis might capture correlations between indicators better.

source_basis: Model validated by SPSS correlation between TAI and GD with significance 0.024.
interpretation: Correlation validates that TAI captures information relevant to match outcomes. However, no out-of-sample test; correlation does not establish causation.
applicability: Correlation validation is common in MCM papers. Pattern: compute composite → correlate with ground truth → report significance.
counterevidence: Cross-validation or holdout test would provide stronger evidence. Regression R-squared not reported.

source_basis: Player ability R2 computed with position-specific AHP weight vectors for F/M/D. Judgment matrices in appendix, CI checks pass.
interpretation: AHP enables position-aware ability quantification. Different positions weighted differently on 5 sub-indicators. CI values (0.1121, 0.0341, 0.0342) all pass.
applicability: Position-specific AHP reusable for any role-differentiated evaluation. Pattern: define sub-indicators → build judgment matrix per role → check consistency.
counterevidence: AHP judgment matrices are inherently subjective despite consistency check. Sensitivity to pairwise comparison values not tested.

source_basis: Four tactical styles classified by 2x2 matrix: possession rate (ours vs theirs) × ball position (our half vs their half) in 15-min windows.
interpretation: Simple classification captures broad tactical patterns. 15-minute granularity from football convention. Hard boundaries between styles may miss gradual transitions.
applicability: 2x2 tactical classification reusable for any strategy-identification task with two binary features.
counterevidence: Fuzzy classification or continuous measures might better capture tactical gradients within 15-min windows.

source_basis: Paper states TAI-GD correlation 'proves that the team can improve TAI value by improving the performance of the six indicators.'
interpretation: Correlation (significance 0.024) does not prove causal mechanism. Improving individual factors may not linearly improve TAI due to potential interactions.
applicability: Common logical error in MCM papers. Pattern: over-interpreting correlation as proof of causal improvement pathway.
counterevidence: Controlled experiments or causal inference methods would be needed to establish causation.

source_basis: Extension from soccer to business/R&D teams based purely on analogy without data or validation.
interpretation: Analogical reasoning without empirical support. Claims that the model 'can be internally extended' are unsubstantiated.
applicability: Generalization sections in MCM papers commonly overreach. Pattern: claim applicability without domain-specific validation.
counterevidence: Domain-specific factors (organizational hierarchy, communication channels) differ substantially from sports passing networks.

source_basis: SPSS correlation confirms TAI-GD positive correlation at p=0.024. Visual confirmation via z-score polygraph and Q-Q diagram.
interpretation: Multiple verification methods (statistical test + two visual checks) strengthen the validation. Significance below 0.05 threshold.
applicability: Multi-method verification pattern reusable: statistical test + visual confirmation via standardized comparison and distributional check.
counterevidence: Sample size (one season of games) may be too small for robust statistical inference.

interpretation: Single-factor fluctuation with others fixed at season average. Confidence intervals show TAI stability under normal variation.
applicability: Single-factor sensitivity with CIs reusable for any composite index. Pattern: fix others at mean, vary one, report confidence intervals.
counterevidence: Multi-factor simultaneous variation not tested; interaction effects could produce larger TAI swings.

source_basis: Tactic counts: BPBC 14, OPSP 89, DPOP 40, LRT 53 over season. Game 30 (12 tactics, 2-0 win) vs Game 9 (0 tactics, 2-5 defeat).
interpretation: Extreme contrast between high-tactic win and zero-tactic loss provides anecdotal validation of micro model.
applicability: Extreme-case contrast reusable for qualitative model validation: compare best and worst outcomes.
counterevidence: Two-game comparison is anecdotal; full season correlation between tactic count and result not computed.

source_basis: MCM-provided passing event data for Huskies full season: passer, receiver, coordinates, timestamps.
interpretation: Standard MCM data package. Third match selected for formation identification. Season-level aggregation for most analyses.
applicability: MCM passing data format reusable across all D-type 2020 papers. Pattern: event-level data → aggregation at match/season level.
counterevidence: Data may contain recording errors or missing events; no data cleaning step described.

source_basis: Field divided into 10x10 zones for computing zone-level passing statistics (mu_z, sigma_z).
interpretation: Zone partition enables spatial analysis of passing distribution. 10x10 grid size not justified; different granularity could change results.
applicability: Zone-based spatial aggregation reusable. Pattern: partition field → compute zonal statistics → use as model input.
counterevidence: Finer grids increase resolution but reduce per-zone sample size. Optimal grid size depends on data density.

source_basis: Particle assumption: players modeled as point masses, ball routes as connections between particles.
interpretation: Standard simplification for network modeling. Ignores player body orientation, sprint direction, and ball trajectory curvature.
applicability: Particle/point-mass assumption common in network-based sports models. Pattern: declare simplification explicitly with named label.
counterevidence: Spatially-aware models using player movement trajectories could capture tactical positioning better.

source_basis: Equal opponent strength: assumes all opponents have comparable overall ability to Huskies.
interpretation: Unrealistic for a full season with varying opponents. Simplifies the adversarial aspect of the evaluation model.
applicability: Equal-strength assumption common in MCM D-type papers when opponent-specific data unavailable.
counterevidence: Opponent strength could be estimated from league standings or historical records.

interpretation: Pezzali score dominates (35.75%), followed by tactical adaptability R3 (18.83%). H indicator least weighted (8.42%). Weight ordering reflects data variance, not importance.
applicability: EWM weight ordering provides insight into which factors vary most across games. Reusable interpretation pattern.
counterevidence: Weights reflect data variance, not causal importance. Low-variance factors may still be critical.

source_basis: Four formation recommendations: use 4-3-3 vs 4-4-2 opponents; don't stick to 4-4-2; prefer five-defender formation; prepare for opponent five-back.
interpretation: Data-driven coaching advice grounded in season-long formation comparison. Practical and actionable.
applicability: Formation recommendation pattern reusable: compare strategy effectiveness across matches, derive conditional suggestions.
counterevidence: Recommendations based on one season; opponent adaptation could invalidate them in subsequent seasons.

source_basis: Best players: F6 (forward), M13 (midfield), D8 (defender) based on AHP ability values. Two optimal squads: 5-4-1 and alternative.
interpretation: Position-specific ranking enables targeted coaching decisions. Two squad compositions provide flexibility.
applicability: Player ranking via composite ability score reusable for any team sport with positional roles.
counterevidence: AHP weights are subjective; different judgment matrices could produce different rankings.

source_basis: Figure 1 flow chart shows work structure: Model 1 → Model 2 → Sensitivity → Suggestions → Generalization.
interpretation: Pipeline visualization aids reader comprehension. Linear structure makes dependency chain explicit.
applicability: Work-flow diagram reusable as paper organization tool. Pattern: one figure summarizing entire methodology pipeline.
counterevidence: Flow chart does not show feedback loops or iterative refinement that may have occurred.

source_basis: References [2], [9], and [11] all cite Cintia et al. 2015 — duplicate bibliography entries.
interpretation: Bibliography management error. Three separate numbered entries for the same paper. Suggests manual rather than automated citation management.
applicability: Duplicate reference detection as quality check. L2 papers sometimes suffer from manual bibliography management.
counterevidence: Automated tools (BibTeX, Zotero) prevent this; their absence indicates manual workflow.

source_basis: MATLAB code in appendix: AHP weight calculation (column normalization, eigenvector, CI) and EWM function skeleton.
interpretation: Code appendix demonstrates reproducibility. AHP code is standard; EWM function incomplete (skeleton only).
applicability: Code appendix pattern reusable: include implementation for key algorithms to support reproducibility claims.
counterevidence: Incomplete EWM function reduces reproducibility value; full implementation would be preferred.
